Summary At the Asean Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Pasay City, there was a collective call to expedite the establishment of the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control to tackle severe haze pollution affecting Southeast Asia.
 The haze, primarily originating from forest fires in Indonesia, has caused disruptions across the region, including in the Philippines.
 Indonesia communicated its ongoing efforts to address the issue, which was received positively by Singapore and Malaysia.
 The dialogue focused on national and regional initiatives to mitigate land and forest fires, aligning with the 2002 Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution.

 Subscribe MANILA, Nov 15 — The foreign ministers of the Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) want to speed up the operationalisation of its coordination centre on transboundary haze control, Philippine News Agency (PNA) reported.
 The renewed call was made during the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Pasay City on Saturday amid growing concerns over severe haze pollution that recently affected several South-east Asian countries.
 Widespread forest fires in Indonesia have triggered severe haze, with thick smog drifting as far as the Philippines and prompting class cancellations in the second half of the year.
 Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said Indonesia, in the meeting, conveyed that it is acting on the issue and exerting its best to address the haze pollution.
 Singapore and Malaysia, she added, were “very cordial” to the statement made by Indonesia.
 “Singapore remarked positively, and Malaysia, the same thing. So, I think that there had been discussions, and perhaps the actions taken by Indonesia was really very sweeping and really helped what is happening,” she said.
 Lazaro said discussions on haze covered ongoing national actions and regional cooperation specifically aimed at mitigating land and forest fires. 
 The regional bloc adopted the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2002 to prevent and monitor transboundary haze pollution caused by land or forest fires.
 Under the deal, the bloc is mandated to put up the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC) to manage the impact of said pollution. — Bernama-Anadolu
